method.cadence: 40+ warmup and 100 measured evaluations per case, three interleaved trials, median of the three trial medians
method.timing: Vulkan timestamp queries bracketing the evaluation; initialization, input uploads and output readback outside them (same exclusions as the NVIDIA CUDA-event probe)
method.inputs: the official probe's inputs recreated byte for byte: SR patterned RGBA16F with zero motion and depth 0.5; RR one static noisy fsr_rr_scene frame with its guides, hit distance 4, view/projection, zero motion, alternating jitter, Reset only on the first evaluation
method.quality: Performance geometry (render half the output per axis); d4r has no separate quality knob in the replay runners
method.not_comparable: whole-evaluation stamps here versus NVIDIA CUDA-event bracketing: both exclude init/upload/readback, but d4r's engine runs one submit with barriers while NGX evaluates on its own; cross-backend arithmetic is native FP8, not NVIDIA's PTX

sr_l_headroom_projection.note: Derived, not measured: d4r M stage times scaled by NVIDIA per-stage L-over-M work ratios, i.e. L costs if its outer stages matched M's relative efficiency.

predicted_l_basis.4k: per-stage scaling of the measured M stages
predicted_l_basis.1440p: M stage sum 1.265 ms scaled by NVIDIA whole-times L/M 1.307 (no 1440p NVIDIA stage profile exists)

sr_l_headroom_projection.why_not_lower: The 1.54x network ratio is shared with M and is hardware-side; matching M's efficiency converges L onto M's 1.12x, not onto NVIDIA's absolute time.

hardware_yardstick.note: Measured peaks on both cards (2026-10-29). Replaces an earlier version that used 811 TFLOPS dense FP8 for the RTX PRO 4500, which is the server edition's sparse figure.

rx_9070_xt.method: HIP v_wmma_f32_16x16x16_fp8_fp8 throughput loop, grid-stride read and copy

rtx_pro_4500_blackwell.method: CUDA mma.sync.m16n8k32 e4m3 (f32 and f16 accumulation) throughput loop, grid-stride read and copy, rented workstation-edition card

rr_d_4k_fraction_of_peak.note: FLOPs estimated from native stage weight layouts; same estimate on both cards

verdicts.stage_class: SR L non-native outer stages (enc0_l, dec0_l)
RR CNN as Vulkan shaders vs native code objects on the same card

valu_measured.note: Vector throughput, same source on both cards (tools/bench_valu.h), independent chains. The FP32 loop compiles to plain v_fma_f32 on RDNA4 (no VOPD dual issue). See docs/amd-vector-issue-limit.md.

limitations: Model version mismatch: local SR M/L are 310.7.0 weights against NVIDIA 310.9.16; local RR D/E/F are 310.9.1 against 310.9.16. RR A/B/C match (310.3.0).
The replay runners have no HDR/auto-exposure creation flags: the SR case runs the engine's exposure stage with the same patterned input, not NGX's auto-exposure path (flags 0x4b).
These are isolated d4r engine evaluations on an RX 9070 XT at a 250 W cap, not game frame times, and not RTX 5070 Ti numbers.

Clocks are not pinned: the sclk DPM state list is dynamic (snapshots of 500/1826/2520 and 500/2765/2520 MHz, rocminfo nominal 2520), sampled per-run medians spanned 1228-3178 MHz, GPU busy averaged 91% and the heaviest runs sat at the 250 W cap (median-of-medians 242 W, maximum sample 352 W).
Cross-backend output differences are arithmetic, not failures: vkhip vs the engine's Vulkan stages is 55-57 dB (SR) and 47.6-49.7 dB (RR at 1440p) / 48.1-50.5 dB (RR at 4K) on this case.
